observation_window.boundary_note: FY2019 flow fields include the pre-cutoff January-April period and are MIXED_CLOCK_CONTEXT rather than clean post-cutoff causal outcomes; event claims only use implementation evidence dated from 2019-05-02 onward.

industry_epoch.condition: National parcel demand was still expanding quickly while concentration, price-service competition, peak capacity and franchise-network stability jointly shaped company outcomes.
industry_epoch.observed_industry_volume: 50.71 billion parcels in FY2018, up 26.6% year on year.
industry_epoch.observed_industry_revenue: RMB 603.84 billion in FY2018, up 21.8% year on year.
industry_epoch.observed_concentration: CR8 was 81.2 in FY2018, up 2.5 points year on year.

mechanism_arenas.mechanism: National e-commerce parcel demand and platform traffic feed shipment volume into competing delivery networks.
mechanism_arenas.value_driver: Parcel adoption, shipper retention, product mix and service-price trade-off.
mechanism_arenas.failure_mode: Industry growth or discounting can be mistaken for customer preference for one network.

mechanism_arenas.mechanism: Self-operated sorting hubs, route planning and trunk capacity convert parcel density into timeliness and unit cost.
mechanism_arenas.value_driver: Sort accuracy, vehicle utilization, route density, peak throughput and fixed-asset productivity.
mechanism_arenas.failure_mode: Capacity additions can raise volume before utilization, service quality or cash returns are proven.

mechanism_arenas.mechanism: Franchisees supply local pickup and delivery capacity while headquarters sets rules, technology, settlement and incentives.
mechanism_arenas.value_driver: Franchisee economics, coverage density, service compliance and network continuity.
mechanism_arenas.failure_mode: Headquarters volume or margin can improve while franchisee economics and service resilience deteriorate.

mechanism_arenas.mechanism: Timeliness, loss and complaint outcomes influence shipper allocation and consumer acceptance alongside price.
mechanism_arenas.value_driver: Complaint rate, on-time delivery, market share and repeat shipper adoption.
mechanism_arenas.failure_mode: Market-share gains alone do not distinguish service improvement from lower price or external demand.

members.cutoff_state: FY2018 parcel volume was 6.985 billion, up 48%; market share was 13.77%; all 55 hubs were self-operated; the network had 3,464 franchisees and 26,149 outlets or service points.
members.decision_heterogeneity: Management emphasized service-led growth, product tiers, automation, route optimization, franchisee enablement and selective property ownership.

members.cutoff_state: FY2018 parcel volume was about 5.112 billion, up about 31.13%; 60 of 68 hubs were self-operated after acquisition of 15 core hubs; the network had 2,233 independent outlets and more than 25,000 service points.
members.decision_heterogeneity: Management was integrating acquired hubs and rebuilding direct control, creating a material perimeter and execution distinction from peers.

members.cutoff_state: FY2018 parcel volume was 6.664 billion, up 31.61%; market share was 13.14%; the network included 67 self-operated hubs, 3,604 franchisees, 29,991 outlets and 12 owned aircraft.
members.decision_heterogeneity: Management combined hub and route optimization with a larger owned-air and international extension, creating a different capital and complexity profile.

strongest_common_rivals: National parcel demand and platform traffic can lift every network.
Price concessions can increase volume and market share without improving customer economics.
New hub capacity and acquired perimeter can lift reported scale before organic execution is established.
Headquarters financial results can diverge from franchisee economics and last-mile resilience.
unresolved_questions: Did service and product differentiation, rather than price or industry growth, explain incremental shipper adoption?
Did automation and route changes improve same-scope unit economics after accounting for parcel mix and network expansion?
Did headquarters growth preserve franchisee health and local service continuity?
Did operating cash fund the required network capital without relying on equity issuance or weakening ordinary-share resilience?
